g.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

text.tspan: /// Represents a single layer of foliage covering the entire world.
/// The layer uses a coordinate-aligned lattice with a fixed value of lattice spacing.
/// The lattice nodes are randomized, and can be further adjusted by overriding [method _place].
/// Lattice spacing for this foliage layer.
/// This should be picked with the size of foliage assets in mind.
/// For example, for trees, a good value is around 16 (the default).
/// For grass / flowers, this can be tuned down to about 2.
/// Each node ends up within a square with linear size 2 * lattice_spacing * randomness,
/// Set this to 0 to place foliage in a rectangular lattice (useful for e.g. crops, vineyards, etc.).
/// Each lattice node will be kept with this probability.
/// Useful to make foliage placement look more natural.
/// If set to a non-negative value, quad tree LODs that are equal or greater to this value
/// will not be instantiated at all. Necessary to avoid generating expensive chunks.
/// For example, you will want to set this to something like 3 for grass, while keeping it
/// Override this function in a script or a subclass to place assets.
/// [b]Warning:[/b] it runs on a worker thread!
/// Whether chunks of this LOD have any foliage of this layer.
/// Builds the hidden chunk node for [param rect], on a worker thread.
/// The node holds a [FoliageMultiMesh] per mesh, and is not added to the tree.
/// Returns [code]null[/code] if the task was cancelled.
// Group the instances by mesh: each mesh becomes one multimesh.
// LOD-(-1) is the first mesh, which turns into scenes up close.
/// Samples the randomized lattice nodes inside [param rect] on the terrain.
/// [b]Warning:[/b] it runs on a worker thread!
// Jitter can move nodes by up to one spacing, so look a bit beyond the rect.
